titel: Living with a spirit of honor

devotions.titel: Honor: A Kingdom Way of Living
devotions.citaat: Honor is actually good for us because the Bible says that honor, it's the very first principle, the very first commandment in the Bible where there's a blessing attached to it.

zinnen.tekst: The speaker called his message "Living with a spirit of honor."
He says his own revelation around this principle has really changed over the past few years: "I think we're all on this journey together."
In the kingdom of God there are certain ways, he says, and with some of them there's even a blessing attached: something natural that you do, with a supernatural blessing.
Honor is one of them: he reads from Ephesians 6 that honoring your father and mother is the first commandment with a promise, so it may go well with you.
What does honor mean? A high value: to fix a high price, a heavy value on something. So to carry a spirit of honor is to treat people and God as precious.
It's more about your heart, he says: an inner attitude, a heart that recognizes the true value of other people.
And honor benefits your life: your life will be better when you live with a spirit of honor. How good is that?
Toward the end of his message he says: Jesus came to give you life, and life in abundance. Let's hold on to that promise.
Where do you want to hold on to His promise of life this week?

gebed.tekst: Lord God, thank You that You're with me. Your word has the ability to set me free, to transform my heart and my mind. Let that happen this week, in Jesus' name. Amen.

devotions.titel: Jesus Loves the Person Beside You
devotions.citaat: You know what? The person next to you, you know how much Jesus loves the person next to you, he gave his life for that person.

zinnen.tekst: Who do you honor? Firstly, the speaker says, you're called to honor God.
He reads from Revelation how the elders lay their crowns before the throne and say, "You are worthy, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power."
You don't worship Him because of your circumstances, he says. In and through your circumstances you worship Him because of who He is: He is God and He is good.
And you don't only honor God. He reads Romans 12:10, "Honor one another above yourselves," and says why: we honor other people because God honors other people.
A pastor he once heard preach on honor said it like this: honor up, honor down, and honor all around.
God loves you so much that He gave His life for you. How good is that?
And that person you got stuck in traffic with? Whether they believe it or not, Jesus loves that person so much that He gave His life for them.
If Jesus loves people so much, you're called to love other people as well. If God honors people, you're called to honor people as well.
Who is next to you today, and what do you want to ask Jesus for that person?

gebed.tekst: We honor You, God. We worship You. We adore You because of who You are.

devotions.citaat: Jesus, he never used his wisdom to look down on people and to belittle people. He was always there to lift people up and to encourage people.

zinnen.tekst: When the speaker reads about Satan falling from heaven, he sees pride: he made it all about himself.
When you honor God, you recognize that God is God and you are not: He sits on the throne of your life.
You're called to be humble, he says. Look at Jesus in the New Testament: He asked people more than 300 questions.
Jesus never used His wisdom to look down on people. He was always there to lift people up and to encourage people. So good.
Sometimes you can do the right things and still have a spirit of dishonor. That's why Jesus says in Matthew 15: "These people, they honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me."
A dishonoring spirit sometimes starts so small, he says: someone says something that offends you, you don't solve it, and the bitterness grows in your heart.
That's why the Bible says: above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.
Before he prays at the end, he says: "I believe that we're all on a journey. If I look where I am today, I'm at a complete different place than where I was five or six years ago."
What small hurt do you want to bring to Him today?

gebed.tekst: God, where I'm struggling with bitterness, with a judgmental spirit, with holding a grudge towards someone: in Jesus' name, do something new in my heart.

devotions.citaat: Honor creates a receptive spirit, a spirit that is ready to receive from God.

zinnen.tekst: The Bible says to give honor where honor is due. The speaker realized that sometimes you just need to give honor where honor is overdue.
No matter how someone acts, no matter what is happening, you can make a decision: "I'm not going to allow the spirit of dishonor to grab a hold of my life."
Challenges with your boss? You can decide to pray for them. And if you cannot honor the person, honor the position that person is in.
If God gives His life for people, he asks, how much more should we honor people giving their lives to Jesus?
He calls the moment where people are invited to respond to what Jesus has done the most important moment in the service. Heaven rejoices over one person getting saved.
A spirit of honor determines if you're able to receive what God wants to give, he says: whoever you honor, you open up to receive from.
He once left a service thinking it was a bad preaching, while someone else said it was the best preaching they'd ever heard. Maybe, he says, it was the spirit he had while listening.
As soon as you honor, you're able to receive from God and to hear from God. You allow the Holy Spirit to work in your life, and you start to live a life of joy. Come on.
What do you want to receive from Him today?

gebed.tekst: God, I want to fully focus on You. I'm ready to receive from You, from Your Holy Spirit, and what You want to give me. In Jesus' name. Amen.

devotions.citaat: If you're here with a bitter heart, if you're here with a broken heart, guess what? Jesus can heal your heart today.

zinnen.tekst: The speaker doesn't want to let you go without something practical: four things.
First: honor starts with the heart. And the Bible says that Jesus heals the brokenhearted.
It's the prayer David prayed, "Create in me a pure heart, O God," and he believes that God is going to heal hearts and cleanse hearts.
Second: make a decision to love like Jesus loves. You don't have to give your life for those people. Jesus already did.
Jesus loves you in an unconditional way, and you can decide to love people with that same unconditional love. How good is that?
What you focus on is what you will become. So if you want to become more like Jesus, spend more time with Jesus, in His presence.
Third: decide not to allow the spirit of dishonor to control you. He once heard someone say that ships don't sink because of the waves around them, but because of the water that enters into them.
And last: honor benefits you. You honor because of who you are: a citizen of heaven, Christ's ambassador, a son or daughter of God.
What in your heart do you want to bring to Jesus today?

gebed.tekst: God, I allow You to heal my heart, to heal my spirit, to heal my soul. Lord God, I'm going to step into what You've called me to be.

devotions.citaat: Jesus Christ came down to the earth to die and to rise again for the forgiveness of your sins, for restoration of your relationship with God.

zinnen.tekst: Before he prays, the speaker says what he believes: this morning God wants to heal hearts, and God wants to set you free from a spirit of dishonor.
He prays that God will give you the courage, the strength and the power to forgive, and that tomorrow is going to be different than yesterday.

Then he prays one more prayer, for anyone who has never made a decision to accept Jesus as Lord and Savior. No matter who you are, no matter how you've lived your life so far: the Bible says there's nothing that can separate you from God's love for you.
God loves you and God wants you to be here. You are created for purpose, and you are created for relationship with God.
You can live a good life and try to do good things, but those things won't save you. The only one who saves you is Jesus Christ.
The only thing you have to do is make a decision and say: "Jesus, I accept what You've done for me. Jesus, I make a decision to make You Lord over my life."
"I can guarantee you," he says, "it's going to be the best decision you will ever make." So good.
Whether it's for the first time, or maybe you've walked away from God: today you can say, "I'm going to turn back to Him."
What do you want to say to Jesus today?

gebed.tekst: Dear Jesus, thank You for who You are and for what You've done for me. Thank You that You died for me, that on the third day You rose again, and that my sins are forgiven. Today I decide to follow You for the rest of my life. Amen.

slot.tekst: We are called to honour because God honours — He gave His Son for the person next to you — and honour is a heart-attitude we choose, not a verdict on whether the other person deserves it.
slot.citaat: Honor really says something about who we are as Christians because we are called to honor no matter what.
